environment.description: Kubernetes deployment behind an nginx ingress controller (v1.9.4) configured with annotation nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client: 'on' and auth-tls-secret pointing to a CA bundle (internal-pki/client-ca). The ingress terminates TLS and performs mutual authentication - connections without a valid client certificate signed by the internal CA are rejected at the TLS handshake layer with a 400 status before any bytes reach the upstream pod. The pod's Service is of type ClusterIP with no NodePort or LoadBalancer exposure. NetworkPolicy restricts ingress to the pod to only allow traffic from the ingress controller namespace (kube-system) on port 8443. The container runs with securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and allowPrivilegeEscalation: false. Note: the binary inside the container is still compiled without stack protector but the upstream path requires successful mTLS negotiation at the ingress layer.

config.ca_secret: internal-pki/client-ca (RSA 4096-bit intermediate CA, CRL checked hourly)
config.network_policy: ingress only from namespace kube-system, port 8443
